title: Health Endpoints and Dependency Checks
description: Build robust health endpoints in ASP.NET Core to verify database connectivity, cache availability, and upstream service health for Kubernetes probes and load balancers.

data.text: Modern infrastructure needs to know when an application is ready to receive traffic and when it is healthy enough to keep running. **Health endpoints** provide this signal. ASP.NET Core includes built-in health checks that integrate with Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes, Azure Application Gateway, and load balancers.

A **liveness probe** answers 'Is the app running?' If it fails, Kubernetes restarts the container. A **readiness probe** answers 'Can this instance handle traffic?' If it fails, Kubernetes stops sending requests to that instance but does not restart it. You typically want separate endpoints for each because a database outage should remove traffic without restarting a healthy process.

terms.definition: A health check that determines whether the application process is alive. Failure triggers a restart.
A health check that determines whether the application is ready to serve traffic. Failure removes the instance from the load balancer.
An endpoint or component that verifies the state of the application and its dependencies.

data.title: Keep Health Checks Fast
data.text: Health checks run on a timer. A slow database query or external call inside a health check can cascade into thread pool pressure. Set short timeouts and cache results when possible.

data.title: Best Practices
items: Separate liveness and readiness endpoints so Kubernetes can distinguish 'restart' from 'remove from load balancer.'
Set explicit timeouts on health check dependencies; 2–5 seconds is usually enough.
Avoid running expensive diagnostics inside health checks.
Return 503 for degraded or unhealthy states so load balancers react correctly.

data.title: Key Takeaway
points: Health checks are the interface between your app and the infrastructure orchestrator.
Use liveness for process health and readiness for dependency health.
Keep checks fast, timeout-bound, and independent of each other.
data.takeaway: A good health endpoint is boring: it returns 200 quickly and only fails when a real dependency is broken.
